memory_candidates.content: In bash under `set -uo pipefail`, expanding a possibly-empty array as `"${arr[@]:-}"` is NOT equivalent to `"${arr[@]}"` when the array is declared-but-empty: the `:-` default form substitutes ONE empty-string WORD (argc=1), while the bare form correctly expands to zero words (argc=0). This matters specifically when the expansion feeds an external command's argument list -- a spurious empty-string argument can be silently rejected by the receiving program's own parser. Confirmed on bash 5.3.9 by direct reproduction. Use the bare `[@]` form (no `:-`) for an array that becomes a command-line argument list; `:-` is only safe for a `for`-loop iterand, where one spurious empty-string iteration is harmless.

gate-cache-lib.sh's implementation-digest component (gate_cache_composite_key -> gate_cache_implementation_digest) requires a COPY of verify-deploy.sh to be physically present under the TARGET fixture directory (at agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/verify-deploy.sh or .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh), used purely to hash a gate's own function body for the composite cache key -- it is never executed. The @extensions corpus resolution also shells out to `git ls-files`, so the fixture must be a real, committed git repository. A test fixture missing either silently resolves the cache key to CANNOT_COMPUTE and the --skip-unchanged write block simply never fires, with no loud error -- easy to misread as 'the narrowing worked' when it actually means 'the cache mechanism never engaged at all'.

update-task-status.sh's `edge_only` target requires `operation:target_status` to resolve to the task's OWN CURRENT status (a no-op replay) -- it is not an unconditional 'just add the edge' call regardless of status. For a task already past `not_started` (e.g. `planned`, `researched`), find the operation:target_status combo that resolves to that SAME current status (e.g. `postflight <task> plan <session_id>` for `planned`) and pass `--depends-on-add` on that call instead of `preflight ... edge_only`.
